correctness.rationale: The nine-monomial multiplication gives (i) an odd-characteristic split conic v^2+2uw=0 and (ii) a characteristic-two two-dimensional leading coefficient space; in either case a pair of nonzero leading vectors has zero product exactly when the vectors are proportional. This yields q+1 mutually nonadjacent peripheral cliques, one universal clique, and all graph parameters. The complete finite-field checks at q=2,3 replay multiplication, squaring, and all ordered pairs; they are consistency tests and not a substitute for the proof. The zero-leading and zero-element boundaries are explicitly counted.

value.rationale: The canonical zero-divisor induced graph on square-zero elements of the nine-dimensional two-generator cubic truncation is a motivated arithmetic invariant, not an arbitrary slice: in characteristic three it is the modular group algebra of C3 x C3. The theorem gives the entire graph up to isomorphism, exact degree partition, clique/chromatic/independence invariants and ordered annihilation-pair census for all finite fields, and exposes an unexpected characteristic-independent graph despite distinct square-zero geometries. It refines the graph-based analysis of modular group algebras; it does not rely on a claimed downstream theorem.
